title: What is (and isn’t) included in a Nile cruise
standfirst: The headline price of a Nile cruise covers less than some people expect and more than others assume. Here is what is usually included, what is not, and what to check before you book. This page is part of our guide to [[up]].

sections.heading: Usually included
paragraphs: Your cabin from check-in on the first day to check-out on the last, and meals on board: most cruises are full board. The sightseeing programme listed for the cruise is often included, with a guide; check whether the guide is shared or private, and whether entrance tickets are covered.

sections.heading: Usually not included
paragraphs: Flights and airport transfers, which you book separately. Drinks, especially alcohol. Optional excursions such as Abu Simbel or a balloon flight. Tombs that need a separate ticket, such as Tutankhamun’s. Your Egypt visa.

sections.heading: Crew gratuities
paragraphs: Gratuities for the crew are obligatory on Nile cruises and are never part of the price. They are paid on board at check-out, at the rate the vessel sets, and at least US$5 per guest per night. Tips for your guide are separate again.

sections.heading: What to check before booking
paragraphs: Whether the sightseeing is included and how it is guided; which entrance tickets are covered; whether drinks are included at meals; and the gratuity rate for the vessel. On Nilecruz each cruise lists what its price includes.

faqs.q: Are drinks included on a Nile cruise?
faqs.a: Water and soft drinks at meals sometimes are; alcohol rarely is. Each cruise lists what is included.
Often, with a guide, but not always, and entrance tickets may be extra. Check the cruise’s inclusions.
